subject: dplyr: Methods for effficient selection of top row in groups

messages.author: ec53b50a5511d439
messages.subject: dplyr: Methods for effficient selection of top row in groups
parts:
Dear all,

A little background:
What I'm trying to do is simply: Group a tbl on a variable, and select the top row in each group (similar to the "mult = 'first'" approach in data.table).

To solve the problem, I started by using the following syntax (using dplyr 0.1.3.99 as of today, April 3):
MyData %.% group_by(myVar) %.% filter(row_number(myVar) ==1)

but that takes a ridiculously long time on a big table (I'm using a 8M row by 7 column tbl_dt).

I've also tried one of the alternative approaches:
MyData %.% group_by(myVar) %.% filter(1:n() == 1)
or
MyData %.% group_by(myVar) %.% filter(row_number() == 1)


but this throws the following errors, respectively:

"Error in n() : This function should not be called directly"
and
"Error in rank(x, ties.method = "first") : 
  argument "x" is missing, with no default"

So now to my question:
It would seem to me that the filter query can be greatly simplified by simply passing the number of the row I want to select as an argument - i.e., using the following query:
MyData %.% group_by(myVar) %.% filter(1)

Is this the desired behavior? And if not - why is that so? It would seem to me that the "1:n()" syntax would simply return a vector of numbers, so why not simply use the first number?

Cheers,
Love Hansson

messages.subject: Re: dplyr: Methods for effficient selection of top row in groups
parts:
Sure!

The dataset below (10M rows, 3 columns) mimics the structure of the dataset I'm working with to some extent (I included the date column for illustration purposes). Note that column MyVar contains >5M different values but that *some* of the values in this column are duplicated. Hence, group_by() creates an extremely large amounts of groups.

MyData <- tbl_dt(
   data.table(
      Id = 1:10000000,
      MyVar = sample(10000000, replace = TRUE),
      someDate = as.POSIXct(sample(10000000, replace = TRUE), origin = Sys.Date())
   )
)

Now, I want to only pick the first row in this data for each by group. The following syntax works, but is extremely slow (~763 seconds on my high-end computer):

FilteredData <- MyData %.%
   group_by(MyVar) %.%
   filter(row_number(MyVar) == 1)

On the other hand, the following query only takes ~5 seconds to execute on the same computer:

FilteredData <- MyData %.%
   group_by(MyVar) %.%
   filter(1)

Also, replacing the query to filter() with the 1:n() syntax results in the error I mentioned in my original post:
"system.time(
+    FilteredData <- MyData %.%
+       group_by(MyVar) %.%
+       filter(1:n() == 1)
+ )
Error in n() : This function should not be called directly"

Thanks for your time and effort,
Love Hansson

Le 3 avr. 2014 à 17:57, Love Hansson <love.h...@gmail.com> a écrit :

Sure!

The dataset below (10M rows, 3 columns) mimics the structure of the dataset I'm working with to some extent (I included the date column for illustration purposes). Note that column MyVar contains >5M different values but that *some* of the values in this column are duplicated. Hence, group_by() creates an extremely large amounts of groups.

MyData <- tbl_dt(
   data.table(
      Id = 1:10000000,
      MyVar = sample(10000000, replace = TRUE),
      someDate = as.POSIXct(sample(10000000, replace = TRUE), origin = Sys.Date())
   )
)

Now, I want to only pick the first row in this data for each by group. The following syntax works, but is extremely slow (~763 seconds on my high-end computer):

FilteredData <- MyData %.%
   group_by(MyVar) %.%
   filter(row_number(MyVar) == 1)

Using the tbl_df backend, that’s 33 seconds in my 4 years old iMac. 

> MyData <- tbl_df(
+    data.frame(
+       Id = 1:10000000,
+       MyVar = sample(10000000, replace = TRUE),
+       someDate = as.POSIXct(sample(10000000, replace = TRUE), origin = Sys.Date())
+    )
+ )
>
>
> system.time( FilteredData <- MyData %.% group_by(MyVar) %.% filter(row_number() == 1) )
utilisateur     système      écoulé
     32.233       0.966      33.578

And this with the data.table back end: 

> system.time( FilteredData <- MyData %.% group_by(MyVar) %.% filter(row_number(MyVar) == 1) )
utilisateur     système      écoulé
    686.823       0.740     688.433

This is likely because we don’t know how to generate the best data.table spell. Some debugging shows that this is what we use:  data[, .I[row_number(MyVar) == 1], by = vars]

On the other hand, the following query only takes ~5 seconds to execute on the same computer:

FilteredData <- MyData %.%
   group_by(MyVar) %.%
   filter(1)
which is mainly the grouping.

Also, replacing the query to filter() with the 1:n() syntax results in the error I mentioned in my original post:
"system.time(
+    FilteredData <- MyData %.%
+       group_by(MyVar) %.%
+       filter(1:n() == 1)
+ )
Error in n() : This function should not be called directly"

The data.table back end probably needs some more code to handle `n()` and generate the appropriate data.table code.  

Romain

Thanks for your time and effort,
Love Hansson

I'm not well versed in the internals of dplyr, but the "spell" you
might be after is simply to not call `row_number` function in this
scenario and just the row number directly as outlined in the
soup-to-nuts example below:

library(dplyr) ## v0.1.3
library(data.table) ## v1.9.2

df <- data.frame(
Id=1:10000000,
MyVar=sample(10000000, replace = TRUE),
someDate=as.POSIXct(sample(10000000, replace = TRUE), origin = Sys.Date()))
tdf <- tbl_df(df)

system.time(fd.dp <- tdf %.%
group_by(MyVar) %.%
filter(row_number(MyVar) == 1))
## user system elapsed
## 35.946 1.076 37.183

dt <- as.data.table(df)
system.time(fd.dt <- dt[ dt[, .I[1], by='MyVar']$V1 ])
## user system elapsed
## 4.227 0.397 4.752

all.equal(fd.dp, as.data.frame(fd.dt))
## [1] TRUE

HTH,
-steve

--
Steve Lianoglou

Genentech
